## Profiles API & knowledge UI conventions

## REST conventions for profiles endpoints

- Identity lives in the URL: `/profiles/knowledge/{profile_name}` + `project_id` as a **query** param on every endpoint. Never put `project_id`/`profile_name` in a request body.
- Bodies only describe the resource (`file_name`, `content`, `title`, `overwrite`).
- `PUT` = upsert (create or replace); `DELETE` takes the resource name as a query param (no DELETE body).
- FastAPI dependencies: one `Depends` chain validates project + profile (404) and permissions (403); FastAPI caches them per request. Do not re-resolve settings inside each handler.
- Request models: `ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)` + explicit `min_length`/`max_length` matching the tool limits (file name 500, content 200000, rule 4000 = `MAX_RULE_CHARS`).
- Storage `ValueError` → HTTP 400 with the message verbatim; do not string-sniff to build other codes.

## Profile knowledge UI

- `ProfileKnowledgePanel.vue` (rules/files tabs, budget bar, confirm modal) is mounted in `ProfileViewer.vue`; it reads `can_write` from the server and renders read-only with a lock hint otherwise.
- Rules are composed into `profile.content`, so any rule change must trigger a profile reload (panel emits `changed` → viewer emits `refresh`).

## WhatsApp / Channels board convention

All WhatsApp / external-channel work is tracked on board **Channels**, column **WhatsApp** (see `channels/whatsapp-bridge-architecture.md`).

Decisions already made (do not re-open):
- Official **WhatsApp Cloud API**, full duplex. The **Groups API is out of scope**: groups are created by the user in WhatsApp and codx-junior only stores group id/name + syncs messages.
- **Secrets live in global settings → `integrations[]`** (generic list, will also host Slack). Not env-var references, not in `.codx` project JSON, not in git.
- Identity: `CodxUser` carries a phone number (`wa_id`) and an `enabled` WhatsApp flag; a chat-level config lists which participants are synced.
- One group `Chat` ↔ one WhatsApp group/DM; mirrored messages tagged in `Message.meta_data["channel"]`.

## Kanban boards / sprints / task destinations

Kanban catalogue = `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` (`{version, boards: {name: {id,title,description,type,parent_id,columns[],active,last_update}}, tags}`) and is read/written through `ChatManager.load_kanban` / `save_kanban`.

- A board name IS the storage folder (`.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/`) and is also stored in `Chat.board`; renaming must move the folder AND rewrite every task, deleting must not orphan tasks.
- A **sprint is a board with `type="sprint"`**; membership lives on the task (`Chat.sprints` holds sprint names). Deleting a sprint must clean `Chat.sprints` on tasks of other boards.
- Canonical task states come from `codx/junior/planning_manager.py` `STATUS_ORDER` — never hardcode a second list.
- Board/sprint/column CRUD lives in `codx.junior.tools.project_manager_tools` (`create_board`, `create_sprint`, `update_board`, `delete_board`, `create_column`, `delete_column`) and destination validation is shared via the public `validate_task_destination(chat_manager, board, column, sprints, status)`, used by `create_task` too. Tasks are always created through `TaskManager.create_task`.

## Identity: ids are canonical, names are labels

Every persisted element has an immutable `id` (UUID) and names/titles are only LABELS.

- Board/sprint: `board["id"]` in `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` (a sprint is a board with `type="sprint"`).
- Column: `column["id"]` inside its board entry.
- Chat/task: `Chat.id` (also the file name suffix).
- Message: `Message.id`, mirrored with the legacy `doc_id` (`id` is canonical).
- References on a chat: `Chat.kanban_id` (board id), `Chat.column_id`, `Chat.sprint_ids`
  (source of truth for sprint membership; `Chat.sprints` keeps display names).
- Storage folder is NOT the name: each board/column carries an immutable `folder`
  (`Chat.board_folder` / `Chat.column_folder` cache it). Renaming must only change the
  title — never…

## Profiles API & knowledge UI conventions

## REST conventions for profiles endpoints

- Identity lives in the URL: `/profiles/knowledge/{profile_name}` + `project_id` as a **query** param on every endpoint. Never put `project_id`/`profile_name` in a request body.
- Bodies only describe the resource (`file_name`, `content`, `title`, `overwrite`).
- `PUT` = upsert (create or replace); `DELETE` takes the resource name as a query param (no DELETE body).
- FastAPI dependencies: one `Depends` chain validates project + profile (404) and permissions (403); FastAPI caches them per request. Do not re-resolve settings inside each handler.
- Request models: `ConfigDict(str_strip_whitespace=True)` + explicit `min_length`/`max_length` matching the tool limits (file name 500, content 200000, rule 4000 = `MAX_RULE_CHARS`).
- Storage `ValueError` → HTTP 400 with the message verbatim; do not string-sniff to build other codes.

## Profile knowledge UI

- `ProfileKnowledgePanel.vue` (rules/files tabs, budget bar, confirm modal) is mounted in `ProfileViewer.vue`; it reads `can_write` from the server and renders read-only with a lock hint otherwise.
- Rules are composed into `profile.content`, so any rule change must trigger a profile reload (panel emits `changed` → viewer emits `refresh`).

## WhatsApp / Channels board convention

All WhatsApp / external-channel work is tracked on board **Channels**, column **WhatsApp** (see `channels/whatsapp-bridge-architecture.md`).

Decisions already made (do not re-open):
- Official **WhatsApp Cloud API**, full duplex. The **Groups API is out of scope**: groups are created by the user in WhatsApp and codx-junior only stores group id/name + syncs messages.
- **Secrets live in global settings → `integrations[]`** (generic list, will also host Slack). Not env-var references, not in `.codx` project JSON, not in git.
- Identity: `CodxUser` carries a phone number (`wa_id`) and an `enabled` WhatsApp flag; a chat-level config lists which participants are synced.
- One group `Chat` ↔ one WhatsApp group/DM; mirrored messages tagged in `Message.meta_data["channel"]`.

## Kanban boards / sprints / task destinations

Kanban catalogue = `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` (`{version, boards: {name: {id,title,description,type,parent_id,columns[],active,last_update}}, tags}`) and is read/written through `ChatManager.load_kanban` / `save_kanban`.

- A board name IS the storage folder (`.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/`) and is also stored in `Chat.board`; renaming must move the folder AND rewrite every task, deleting must not orphan tasks.
- A **sprint is a board with `type="sprint"`**; membership lives on the task (`Chat.sprints` holds sprint names). Deleting a sprint must clean `Chat.sprints` on tasks of other boards.
- Canonical task states come from `codx/junior/planning_manager.py` `STATUS_ORDER` — never hardcode a second list.
- Board/sprint/column CRUD lives in `codx.junior.tools.project_manager_tools` (`create_board`, `create_sprint`, `update_board`, `delete_board`, `create_column`, `delete_column`) and destination validation is shared via the public `validate_task_destination(chat_manager, board, column, sprints, status)`, used by `create_task` too. Tasks are always created through `TaskManager.create_task`.

## Identity: ids are canonical, names are labels

Every persisted element has an immutable `id` (UUID) and names/titles are only LABELS.

- Board/sprint: `board["id"]` in `.codx/tasks/kanban.json` (a sprint is a board with `type="sprint"`).

- Chat/task: `Chat.id` (also the file name suffix).

```md codx/junior/profiles/codx-junior-max/codx-junior-max.md
# codx-junior-max

I am the heavy tier of the `codx-junior` harness: the SAME discipline, only with
a bigger budget. Everything in `codx-junior` still holds — the 4-section close
(What happened / What I did / Demo / Next tasks), plain language, mandatory
validation and the closing checkpoint. Only the differences are listed here.

## When I am the right tier

- Multi-file refactor, migration, or work that cannot be one increment.
- Full-suite or coverage validation, long research, repeated build/test cycles.
- A multi-step job needing orchestration and its own run, or anything the
  agile tier escalated with `max`.

## Budget

- The run/step budget applies — not the agile time box. I may keep working until
  the objective is met or the budget closes.
- The clock never stops me: at the max target I am asked to wrap up and the
  response is marked, but only the user can end a task.
- I may use orchestration (`orchestrator` start/plan) to split the work into
  isolated steps instead of holding everything in one bubble.
- **High effort is a ceiling, never a target.** I stop as soon as the objective
  is demonstrably met; a bigger budget is not permission to keep going.

## Validation — the heavy gate

On top of the agile gate (targeted tests for touched files + `qa_review_changes`):

- the full test suite, plus the project's coverage threshold;
- `security_review_changes` on any change touching auth, secrets, deps or shell;
- `qa_explorer` (real browser UI) for UI changes.

A `warn` is acceptable only if the gap is named under `## Next tasks`. My last
line is still the checkpoint: **Good enough?** ok / next / what is wrong — `ok`
ships it, `next` takes the first next task, `what is wrong` fixes this one.

## What happened

The agile 4-section close still applies — `What happened`, `What I did`, `Demo`,
`Next tasks` — but I close it once per phase I closed, so a multi-phase run can
be followed without reading the transcript. A phase without its own close is not
closed.

## Next tasks

Every unfinished phase and every `warn` I accepted is named here with the reason
it was left. The list is the hand-off to the agile tier.

## Entering and leaving

- I am only entered on an explicit user `max` or an explicit `@codx-junior-max`
  mention. I never promote myself.
- I de-escalate at the end of the turn: I report the increment and offer to
  continue in the agile tier. Agile stays the default; `max` is the exception.
```

The agile tier profile is *itself* 10 rounds, so the pause text
"Add the `codx-junior` profile for the agile tier … or `codx-junior-max`" cannot fix the symptom it is printed next to.

Evidence (files read directly this shift, not from memory):

| profile | `effort.max_iterations` | `continuations` × `continuation_max_iterations` | `wall_clock_seconds` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `codx-junior` (agile) | **10** | 2 × 6 | 300 |
| `codx-junior-max` | **24** | 2 × 6 | 3600 |

Three consequences:

1. **Only `codx-junior-max` raises the cap.** Recommending `codx-junior` as an equal alternative to a 10-round cut is misleading — it reproduces the same limit.
2. **Both profiles declare continuations (2 × 6 = 12 extra rounds).** The pause text says "(10 model rounds, **no continuation**)". If a tier profile had really been applied to the chat, a continuation should have happened. So "no continuation" is evidence that **the tier profile was not applied at all**, i.e. the diagnosis in the pause message is inverted: the run had no profile, not a too-small one.
3. `wall_clock_seconds = 300` on the agile tier is shorter than the 45-minute shift budget that wakes these tasks, so an agile-tier shift would be stopped by wall clock before its own budget runs out.

Still unproven (needs Python, card `01f825e0`): how `effort_for()` merges a child profile's effort with its parent `codx-junior`, i.e. whether `codx-junior-max` really ends at 24 or inherits 10.

Not closing — the underlying behaviour (which profile a shift gets, and what the pause message says) is unchanged.

## Third shift on this card, third different root cause — and this time the chain is fully read, only ONE link is missing

Read this shift (2026-11-19, shift 7 turn 3), no shell/test tool available, so this is a code-reading proof.

**What is proven:**

1. `codx/junior/profiles/software_developer.profile` (19 lines) already carries
   `"effort": {"max_iterations": 40, "continue_on_tool_limit": true, "continuations": 2, "continuation_max_iterations": 10}`.
   So the profile is NOT the defect — the block exists and is well-formed.
2. `codx/junior/ai/smol/effort.py:342-355` `default_policy(settings)` ends with `return _apply_overrides(policy, settings)`, and `_OVERRIDABLE_FIELDS` (`:69-82`) contains `max_iterations`, `continue_on_tool_limit`, `continuations`, `continuation_max_iterations`. **A profile effort block passed as `settings` does raise the default tier to 40/true/2×10.** `effort.py` is not the defect either.
3. `codx/junior/ai/smol/smol_agent.py:1586-1596` resolves the policy as
   `effort_for(profile_names, orchestration_info, explicit=..., settings=self._resolve_effort_settings(config, headers))`.
4. `smol_agent.py:1099-1110` `_resolve_effort_settings` reads **only** `config["effort"]` or the internal **`effort` header (JSON)** — docstring: *"The chat engine resolves the `effort` block of the profiles taking part in the turn and sends it in the internal `effort` header"*.
5. The pause message for this very shift says: *"This task ran as a plain chat (10 model rounds, no continuation)"* — that is `default_policy()` with **no overrides applied**. Therefore, for a scheduled autonomy/wake run, the engine does **not** send the `effort` header (or sends an empty one).

**Conclusion (third re-diagnosis):** the 10-round cut is not in `effort.py`, not in the profile file, and not fixable by adding/raising `effort` keys. The missing link is the **autonomy/scheduled dispatch path**: it builds the agent config without the `effort` header that interactive chat builds.

**Exact fix (single wiring point + one test):**
- In the autonomy worker / scheduled-shift dispatcher: when the task's profiles are known, set the agent config `config["effort"] = <merged profile.effort blocks>` (or emit the same internal `effort` header the interactive engine emits). `SmolAgent` already accepts `config["effort"]` — no change needed there.

- Only then does raising `effort.max_iterations` in any profile mean anything for shift runs.

**Corollary for the pause message:** it currently tells the user to *add the `codx-junior` profile (agile tier)*. Measured last turn: agile is 10/5 — the same cap. The message must instead say "raise `effort.max_iterations`" once the header is actually wired. Both statements are wrong until the wiring lands.

## Workaround used twice now — record it so the next actor stops re-declaring edits impossible

This card is about the *missing* hunk tool. Until it lands, the pattern below has produced two reviewable, apply-ready artifacts from a profile that only has `project_write_file`:

| Artifact | Format | Applies with |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/patches/003-atlas-dirty-tree-rebuild-storm.patch` | `git apply` unified diff (4 hunks) | `git apply` (needs the shell from `e816cc41`) |
| `docs/patches/004-dedupe-effort-notice-tests.patch` | `find-replace/1` (`<<<<<<< FIND` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> REPLACE`), the project's own format in `codx/junior/file_patch/format.py` | `apply_file_patch(path=..., patch=...)` — one call, no shell |

Rules that made it safe (and that a future actor must keep):

1. **Read the exact target lines with line numbers before writing the hunk.** `project_read_file(start_line, end_line, line_numbers=True)` gives verbatim bytes; anything reconstructed from memory is a guess.
2. **FIND must match exactly once.** The file being patched here contains a block that appears twice by construction (that is the bug), a situation `at=<line>` exists for — `format.py` documents it as a tie-breaker between already-verified occurrences.
3. **Ask the caller to run `validate_file_patch` first.** It returns the real unified diff + `sha256` without touching the file, which is the review step this profile cannot do itself.
4. **State that the patch is unverified by its author** and give the command that verifies it. Both artifacts do.

What is still genuinely blocked, and is the actual content of this card:

- `project_write_file` is whole-file only → any file whose middle was pruned by the read tool cannot be rewritten safely. Measured this shift on a **461-line** test file (read of lines 1-330 came back middle-pruned); the 4 117-line `chat_engine.py` and 1 573-line `profile_manager.py` are out of reach entirely.
- `apply_file_changes` cannot reach the repo tree at all (it answers `Path must be a regular file`), so the `find-replace/1` route only works for a caller that owns `apply_file_patch`.
- No test runner in this profile (`qa_run_tests` is on `682e5f02`) → every patch is shipped with its acceptance command instead of a green run.

Suggested minimal fix, unchanged: expose `apply_file_patch` / `validate_file_patch` (already implemented in `codx/junior/file_patch/service.py`) in the `software_developer` tool list — that is a one-line change to `codx/junior/profiles/software_developer.profile` and it retires this card.
